QuestionStmt.S: When a resistance of 200 Ω is connected in series with a galvanometer of resistance G, its range is V. To triple its range, a resistance of 2000 Ω is connected in series. The value of G is

Solution.S:
For a galvanometer converted to voltmeter, the range is V = I_g (G + R).

Case 1: R₁ = 200 Ω, range = V.

V = I_g (G + 200) ... (i)

Case 2: Range is tripled, so new range = 3V, with R₂ = 2000 Ω.

3V = I_g (G + 2000) ... (ii)

Divide (ii) by (i):

$$\frac{3V}{V} = \frac{G + 2000}{G + 200}$$

$$3 = \frac{G + 2000}{G + 200}$$

$$3G + 600 = G + 2000$$

$$2G = 1400 \Rightarrow G = 700 \Omega$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{700 \Omega}$$

Hence, the correct option is C.
